drafts.title: Benchmarking 10 LLMs on MacBook Air M1 (8GB RAM): Qwen3 4B Took Over 8 Minutes to Generate a Single Math Question
drafts.body: A recent benchmark tested 10 different large language models (LLMs) locally on a MacBook Air M1 with 8GB of RAM, using quantized versions configured with specific Ollama environment variables. The methodology involved each model generating one question on five topics (Math, Writing, Coding, Psychology, History), answering all 50 generated questions, and then evaluating every answer, including their own. A striking finding was that the Qwen3 4B model took 486 seconds—more than 8 minutes—to generate a single math question, highlighting significant performance variability on limited-memory hardware. Additionally, several models such as Mistral, Qwen3, and LLaMA 3.1 8B showed a tendency to overrate their own answers, indicating self-evaluation bias. The author noted that model size did not directly correlate with performance, emphasizing that bigger models aren't always better for constrained devices. While Gemma3:latest was identified as a consistent and numerically stable scorer, these assessments are subjective and based on this specific hardware and quantized setup. This benchmark underscores the challenges and trade-offs when running LLMs locally on low-spec machines like the M1 MacBook Air with limited RAM.

drafts.title: Benchmarking 10 LLMs on a MacBook Air M1 (8GB RAM) Reveals Huge Speed Differences and Self-Evaluation Biases
drafts.body: A recent benchmark tested 10 quantized large language models (LLMs) locally on a MacBook Air M1 with 8GB RAM to evaluate their performance under tight hardware constraints. Each model generated one question across five topics—Math, Writing, Coding, Psychology, and History—then answered all 50 questions and self-evaluated their responses. Notably, the Qwen3 4B model took 486 seconds (over 8 minutes) just to generate a single math question, highlighting significant speed variability among models. Several models, including Mistral, Qwen3, and LLaMA 3.1 8B, showed a tendency to overrate their own answers, indicating self-evaluation biases. These results underline that running LLMs locally on low-spec hardware is feasible but performance and evaluation quality vary widely. Users should consider these factors, along with the limitations of a single-user test and specific quantized setups, when selecting models for local deployment.

drafts.title: 在MacBook Air M1（8GB内存）上对10个LLM进行基准测试：Qwen3 4B生成单个数学问题耗时超过8分钟
drafts.body: 最近的一项基准测试在配备8GB内存的MacBook Air M1上本地测试了10个不同的大型语言模型（LLM），使用了量化版本并配置了特定的Ollama环境变量。方法论包括每个模型在五个主题（数学、写作、编码、心理学、历史）上各生成一个问题，回答所有50个生成的问题，然后评估每个答案，包括它们自己的。一个显著的发现是Qwen3 4B模型生成单个数学问题耗时486秒——超过8分钟，凸显了有限内存硬件上的性能差异。此外，多个模型如Mistral、Qwen3和LLaMA 3.1 8B表现出高估自身答案的倾向，显示了自我评估偏差。作者指出模型大小与性能不直接相关，强调更大的模型并不总是适合受限设备。虽然Gemma3:latest被认为是一个一致且数值稳定的评分者，但这些评估是主观的，基于特定硬件和量化设置。该基准测试强调了在低规格机器如M1 MacBook Air有限内存上本地运行LLM时的挑战和权衡。

drafts.title: 在MacBook Air M1（8GB内存）上对10个LLM进行基准测试揭示巨大速度差异和自我评估偏差
drafts.body: 最近的一项基准测试在配备8GB内存的MacBook Air M1上本地测试了10个量化大型语言模型（LLM），以评估它们在硬件受限条件下的性能。每个模型在五个主题——数学、写作、编码、心理学和历史——上各生成一个问题，然后回答所有50个问题并自我评估其回答。值得注意的是，Qwen3 4B模型仅生成一个数学问题就耗时486秒（超过8分钟），凸显了模型间显著的速度差异。多个模型，包括Mistral、Qwen3和LLaMA 3.1 8B，表现出高估自身答案的倾向，显示了自我评估偏差。这些结果表明，在低规格硬件上本地运行LLM是可行的，但性能和评估质量差异很大。用户在选择本地部署模型时应考虑这些因素，以及单用户测试和特定量化设置的局限性。
